newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Lackluster day for new issues.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Lackluster day for new issues.

text.p: The three initial public offerings that came to market on Friday priced either at the low end of their estimated range or below it, signalling dampened demand.
Omniquip International Inc's eight million share deal priced at $14, at the bottom of the $14 to $16 range, and moved up 1/2 in late afternoon trading. The lead manager was Morgan Stanley.

The Port Washington, Wis.-based company manufactures telescopic material handlers, as well as a line of skid steer loaders and a limited range of other material handling equipment. It had net sales of $124.9 million for the fiscal year ended September 30,1996.
Cell Therapeutics Inc's offering priced at $10 a share, significantly below the $14 to $16 range indicated in the company's filing. Shares gained 1/8 to reach 10-1/8.

The Seattle-based company is focused on the discovery, development and commercialization of small molecule drugs for the treatment of cancer and inflammatory and immune diseases. UBS Securities was lead underwriter for the issue.

Shares of Physicians' Specialty Corp priced at $8 each, and slipped lower to 7-7/8 by late afternoon. The estimated price range on the 2.2 million share deal, lead-managed by Southcoast Capital Corp, was $8 to $9 a share.
The company, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, provides management services to medical groups specializing in ear, nose and throat disorders.
